info.name: FynnEdge Advisory API (v1)
info.description:
The API the FynnEdge Flutter application talks to. Every endpoint here
answers for one authenticated customer, from their own stored records.

**Authentication.** There are no passwords. A customer is a mobile
number that proves itself with a one-time code: `POST /auth/send-otp`
then `POST /auth/verify-otp` returns a Sanctum bearer token, which
every other endpoint requires as `Authorization: Bearer <token>`.
Tokens last 30 days and are revoked per device.

**Ownership.** A customer-scoped record that belongs to somebody else
answers **404, not 403** — deliberately, so that a caller cannot tell
"not yours" from "does not exist".

**Not connected.** Credit checks, lender submission, identity
verification, document reading and push delivery have no provider
configured in this deployment. Those endpoints answer **501** with a
machine-readable `reason`, rather than simulating a result.

Examples use reserved test numbers and invented data throughout.

---

**Generated from the OpenAPI document, which is generated from the routes.** Every request here corresponds to one of the 82 live API routes.

### Getting a token

1. Set `baseUrl` and `mobile` in the collection variables.
2. Run **Authentication → send-otp**. Its script stores the `reference` that verify-otp requires, and on a local build it also fills in `otp` from the development hint.
3. Run **Authentication → verify-otp** — its script stores the returned token as `token`.

In production there is no development hint: the code only reaches the handset, so set `otp` yourself between the two steps.

Every other request inherits `Authorization: Bearer {{token}}` from the collection.

### Requests that need a product

**Products & Matching → products** stores the first catalogue entry as `product_id`. Run it once and *compare*, *fynn-twin/simulate* and *applications* will work as they are.

### Path variables

Requests with `:id`-style segments expose them under the request's **Path Variables** tab. They are left empty on purpose — fill them with ids from a list endpoint. Asking for a resource that belongs to someone else returns **404**, not 403: that is deliberate, and not a bug.

No credentials, tokens or OTP values are stored in this file.

GET /decisions

The history, newest first. Empty for a customer who has explored
nothing — and empty is the honest answer, not a prompt to go and do
something.

GET /decisions/{decision}

One entry with its explanation. The explanation is built from what
was recorded at the time, so a decision from six months ago explains
itself with the rate it was actually shown.

GET /intelligence

The state read once and handed to both rule sets, so the insight and
the next action cannot disagree about the customer.

GET /intelligence/timeline

The customer's financial story, newest first. Not the audit log:
nothing here is a webhook, a retry, a storage operation or a consent
record.

The app compares locally so the maths stays consistent offline; this
endpoint exists for server-side consumers and audit trails

request.description:
The app compares locally so the maths stays consistent offline; this
endpoint exists for server-side consumers and audit trails

DELETE /applications/{application}/documents/{requirement}

Removes the choice. The document itself stays in the vault, untouched.

GET /applications/{application}/documents

The checklist, recomputed from what is true now — so a document
deleted from the vault shows as missing the moment anybody looks.

GET /applications/{application}/submission

Where the external submission stands. Never calls a provider, so
opening the screen cannot send anything.

POST /applications/{application}/documents

Chooses one of the customer's vault documents for a requirement.
Choosing is not confirming: the slot becomes "needs your
     * confirmation", and they still have to say it is the right one.

POST /applications/{application}/documents/{requirement}/review

The customer's decision: this is the document to use, or it is not.

Accepting is the customer confirming their own choice. It is not
verification by FynnEdge, not approval, and nobody outside FynnEdge
has seen the document.

POST /applications/{application}/submission

Sends it, because the customer asked with the destination in front of
them. There are no body parameters at all: the provider, the outcome
and the simulated flag are server- and provider-owned, and an
application id in the body would reach nothing.

Asks the bureau, if the customer has permitted it

Returns a report already held when one is recent enough, rather than
paying for and recording another enquiry.

GET /documents/{document}/kyc

What FynnEdge already knows. Never asks a provider, so opening the
screen cannot cost the customer a charge.

GET /documents/{document}/scan

What FynnEdge already knows. Never asks a provider, so opening the
screen cannot cost the customer a charge.

POST /documents/{document}/kyc

Asks for the document to be checked, because the customer asked.

POST /documents/{document}/kyc/resolve

What the customer decides about a difference: their profile is right,
or the document is and they want their profile corrected.

Deliberately the only path by which a verification can change a
profile, and it runs only when a customer chooses one of these.

POST /documents/{document}/scan

Asks for the document to be read, because the customer asked.

POST /documents/{document}/scan/review

The customer's answer about one field: it is right, it is wrong and
here is the right figure, or it is wrong and they are not supplying
one. Optionally, and only when they ask, the confirmed figure is
carried into their financial profile.

query.description:
The id of the oldest notification already held. Ids descend,
so "older than this" is a single indexed comparison and does
not drift when something new arrives mid-scroll the way an
offset would.

request.description:
GET /notifications

Newest first, a page at a time. The unread count travels in the meta
so the badge does not cost a second request, and it counts rather
than loads: it is never derived from the page.

GET /notifications/unread-count

One number, one indexed count. Home asks for this and nothing else,
so a badge never costs a page of notifications.

POST /notifications/devices

Registering a token that is already registered to somebody else
moves it. That is correct rather than permissive: a handset belongs
to whoever is signed in on it, and leaving the previous registration
active would send one customer's notifications to a phone another
customer is holding.

POST /notifications/read-all

Safe to repeat, and scoped by the relation — one customer's read-all
cannot reach another's rows, because the update is issued through
their own relation rather than against the table.

POST /notifications/{notification}/read

Idempotent: reading something twice leaves the first read_at alone,
so the time shown is when they actually first saw it.
GET /support/cases — newest first

GET /support/categories

What a customer can ask about, in the order they are offered. Labels
come from the enum so the app never spells one differently.

POST /support/cases

Idempotent on the Idempotency-Key header, the same as an application:
a customer tapping "Get help" twice has asked once.

POST /support/cases/{case}/close

The customer no longer needs help. Recorded with a reason, so a
request they closed is distinguishable from one FynnEdge resolved.

POST /support/cases/{case}/messages

The customer adds something. Authored as the customer by the server,
always — there is no field for who wrote it.

Answers one message

With no assistant configured this answers 501 rather than inventing a
reply or quietly handing the question to something the customer was
not told about.
